definitions.gloss: touting; soliciting customers on the street
definitions.explanation: The act of approaching people on the street to invite them into a shop, restaurant, or establishment.
A person who stands outside a business and tries to attract customers by calling out to passersby. Common in entertainment districts.

examples.japanese: {客引|きゃくひ}きは{禁止|きんし}されている。
{駅前|えきまえ}で{居酒屋|いざかや}の{客引|きゃくひ}きをしている{人|ひと}がいた。
examples.english: There was someone touting for an izakaya in front of the station.

examples.japanese: しつこい{客引|きゃくひ}きに{困|こま}った{経験|けいけん}がある。
examples.english: I have had the experience of being bothered by persistent touting.

examples.japanese: {客引|きゃくひ}きに{声|こえ}をかけられた。
examples.english: I was approached by a tout.

examples.japanese: {繁華街|はんかがい}には{客引|きゃくひ}きが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many touts in the entertainment district.

examples.japanese: {客引|きゃくひ}きの{誘|さそ}いには{乗|の}らないほうがいいと{地元|じもと}の{人|ひと}に{言|い}われた。
examples.english: A local told me it's better not to follow the touts' invitations.

notes:
USAGE:
{客引|きゃくひ}き combines {客|きゃく} (customer) and {引|ひ}き (pulling). It can refer to either the act of soliciting or the person doing it. {客引|きゃくひ}きをする means to tout or solicit. In many Japanese cities, aggressive touting is regulated or banned by local ordinances.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {客引|きゃくひ}きをする (to tout, to solicit customers)
- {客引|きゃくひ}き{禁止|きんし} (touting prohibited)
- {客引|きゃくひ}きに{声|こえ}をかけられる (to be approached by a tout)
- しつこい{客引|きゃくひ}き (persistent touting)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{呼|よ}び{込|こ}み refers to barkers calling out to attract customers, often at markets or street stalls. {客引|きゃくひ}き has a more negative connotation and is associated with nightlife districts.
